docs.title: SOMA
docs.text: A LinkML schema for representing Key Event and Outcome measurements, assays, and experimental protocols in the context of environmental health sciences (EHS) outcomes research.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This data model provides a standardized way to capture and exchange data about airway biology assays relevant to respiratory health outcomes, including:

  • Ciliary function - Beat frequency, active area, morphology
  • Airway surface liquid - ASL height, periciliary layer depth, ion composition
  • Mucociliary clearance - Transport rates, directionality, clearance efficiency
  • Oxidative stress - ROS, lipid peroxidation, antioxidant capacity
  • Ion channel function - CFTR chloride secretion, sweat chloride
  • Signaling pathways - EGFR phosphorylation, downstream kinases
  • Mucin biology - Goblet cells, MUC5AC/MUC5B expression
  • Inflammatory markers - BALF/sputum cell counts, cytokines
  • Lung function - Spirometry outcomes (FEV1, FVC)
  • Gene expression - Target gene mRNA levels

docs.title: Assay-Centric Architecture
docs.text: The schema uses an assay-centric architecture where domain-specific assay types inherit from a common Assay base class. Each assay class has named measurement slots (e.g., beat_frequency_hz, asl_height_um) instead of generic observation types.

docs.title: Assay Microschemas
docs.text: Assay Class Container Slot Description CiliaryFunctionAssay ciliary_function_assays Ciliary beat frequency, active area, morphology ASLAssay asl_assays Airway surface liquid height, PCL depth, ions MucociliaryClearanceAssay mcc_assays Mucociliary transport and clearance OxidativeStressAssay oxidative_stress_assays ROS, MDA, lipid peroxidation CFTRFunctionAssay cftr_assays CFTR chloride secretion, sweat chloride EGFRSignalingAssay egfr_signaling_assays EGFR/ERK/AKT phosphorylation GobletCellAssay goblet_cell_assays Goblet cells, MUC5AC/5B expression BALFSputumAssay balf_sputum_assays Cell differentials, cytokines LungFunctionAssay lung_function_assays FEV1, FVC, FeNO FoxJExpressionAssay foxj_assays FoxJ1 expression, ciliogenesis GeneExpressionAssay gene_expression_assays Target gene mRNA expression

docs.title: Study Subject Hierarchy
docs.text:
Each assay records its biological system via the study_subject slot, which accepts any class in the StudySubject hierarchy. The hierarchy has exactly three subclasses — one for each kind of thing a study can be performed on:

Class Use Case Key Slots StudySubject Base class species ModelSystem Laboratory model systems (inherits from StudySubject) CellularSystem Cell-based experiments cell_type, cell_line, culture_conditions, days_at_differentiation, substrate_type, passage_number InVivoSubject Human/animal samples age, sex, sample_type, collection_site, subject_characteristics PopulationSubject Epidemiological cohorts cohort_name, sample_size, demographics

Every study subject records its species in the species slot — a human cohort records Homo sapiens there just as a cell line records its species of origin.

docs.title: Ontology Term References
docs.text:
Classes named *Reference are not study subjects or experimental entities — they are small value holders (an ontology identifier plus its label) used as the range of descriptive slots. They all inherit from NamedEntity. The schema has two parallel root classes: NamedThing (id, name, description) for first-class records such as assays, study subjects, protocols, and key events, and NamedEntity (id, name) for the descriptive value objects that live inside those records' slots. Not every NamedEntity is an ontology-term pointer — some subclasses, like ExposureCondition and CellLine, are things the schema itself defines, optionally mapped to ontology terms — but the *Reference classes are pure term pointers:

Reference Class Ontology Used By (for example) SpeciesReference NCBI Taxonomy species on StudySubject, CellLine CellTypeReference Cell Ontology (CL) cell_type, target_cell_type AnatomicalEntityReference UBERON anatomical_origin ChemicalEntityReference ChEBI / ECTO / ENVO exposure_agent

For example, SpeciesReference is how a study subject's species slot points at an NCBI Taxonomy term; it is not a fourth kind of study subject.

docs.title: Protocol Hierarchy
docs.text:
Assays reference typed protocols for domain-specific procedural details:

Protocol Class Slot Name Key Slots Protocol follows_protocols protocol_version, temperature_control, quality_control_criteria, sub_protocols ImagingProtocol imaging_protocol imaging_frame_rate, imaging_duration, spatial_resolution MolecularAssayProtocol molecular_protocol detection_method, antibodies_used, reference_gene StainingProtocol staining_protocol staining_type, fixation_method, counterstain SpirometryProtocol spirometry_protocol spirometry_standard, bronchodilator_agent

Assays reference protocols via follows_protocols (multivalued — an assay can follow multiple protocols). Protocols can compose other protocols via sub_protocols (e.g., sample prep, wash steps, post-processing). Any Protocol subclass is valid in both slots.

docs.title: Supporting Entities
docs.text: Entity Container Slot Description Protocol protocols Detailed experimental procedures KeyEvent key_events AOP key events that assays inform on AdverseOutcome adverse_outcomes Outcomes, grounded to MONDO/HPO terms AdverseOutcomePathway adverse_outcome_pathways Complete AOP definitions

docs.title: From an Outcome to Relevant Assays
docs.text: An AdverseOutcome is a specialized KeyEvent, so it inherits upstream_key_events, and its outcome_term slot grounds it to a MONDO disease or HPO phenotype term. This closes the Outcome ↔ Key Event ↔ Assay traversal: to answer "I am looking for data on this outcome — what assays might be relevant?", find the outcome by its ontology term, walk its upstream_key_events, and collect every assay whose informs_on_key_event matches the outcome itself or any Key Event in the chain. No curated AdverseOutcomePathway record is required. See Container-outcome_connection.yaml in the examples for a worked traversal.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
The schema integrates with major biomedical ontologies:

Domain Ontologies Biological Processes GO (Gene Ontology) Chemicals ChEBI Phenotypes HP (Human Phenotype Ontology) Cell Types CL (Cell Ontology) Environment ENVO Units UO, UCUM, QUDT Assays OBI

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The schema can be used to:

  1. Validate data - Ensure your data conforms to the model
  2. Generate code - Create Python dataclasses, Pydantic models, JSON Schema
  3. Transform data - Convert between JSON, YAML, RDF, and other formats

docs.title: The SOMA
docs.text: The SOMA is part of the EHS Data Standards initiative, focused on developing standardized data models for environmental health sciences research.

docs.title: Project Goals
docs.text:
This project aims to:

  1. Standardize data representation for exposure-outcome relationships in EHS research
  2. Enable data interoperability across studies, cohorts, and institutions
  3. Support mechanistic understanding through integration with Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs)
  4. Bridge epidemiological and toxicological data from human studies and model systems

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
The SOMA follows these principles:

  • Ontology-first - All entities are mapped to established biomedical ontologies
  • FAIR-compliant - Supports Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable data
  • Extensible - New assay types can be added without breaking existing data
  • Multi-scale - Captures data from molecular to population levels

docs.title: Technology Stack
docs.text:
The model is built using:

  • LinkML - Linked Data Modeling Language for schema definition
  • MkDocs with Material theme for documentation
  • Python for data validation and transformation

docs.title: Core Domains
docs.text: Domain Description Assays Domain-specific assay classes with named measurement slots (e.g., CiliaryFunctionAssay, LungFunctionAssay) Study Subjects Biological systems under study: cell cultures (CellularSystem), human/animal subjects (InVivoSubject), populations (PopulationSubject) Protocols Typed experimental procedures: ImagingProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol AOP Framework Adverse Outcome Pathways: KeyEvent, AdverseOutcomePathway, with assay linkage via informs_on_key_event

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
We welcome contributions from the community. To contribute:

  1. Visit the GitHub repository
  2. Review the existing schema in src/soma/schema/
  3. Open an issue to discuss proposed changes
  4. Submit a pull request with your contributions

docs.title: Development
docs.text: For local development, use uv and just as the canonical entry points. The repository may contain underlying Python, npm, and LinkML commands, but contributors should treat the just recipes as the supported interface for routine setup, testing, and generation tasks.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10+
  • uv for Python environment and dependency management
  • just for repository task automation
  • node and npm for DataHarmonizer frontend builds

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Install the Python dependencies managed by the repo:

just install

docs.title: Common Commands
docs.text:
• Run the full validation workflow: just test
  • Regenerate project artifacts: just gen-project
  • Regenerate schema documentation: just gen-doc
  • Build the DataHarmonizer assets: just build-dh
  • Run the local documentation server: just testdoc
  • List all available recipes: just --list

If you need to run a Python tool directly, prefer uv run ... so it executes inside the managed project environment.

docs.title: Paper-Derived SOMA Data
docs.text: SOMA-conformant data extracted from published PM2.5 research papers. Each workbook contains assay measurements mapped to the SOMA schema with full provenance (figure/table references, p-values, protocols, exposure conditions).

docs.title: Montgomery et al. (2020)
docs.text:
"Genome-Wide Analysis Reveals Mucociliary Remodeling of the Nasal Airway Epithelium Induced by Urban PM2.5"

Am J Respir Cell Mol Biol. 2020;63(2):172-184 | Paper | PubMed Central | DOI: 10.1165/rcmb.2019-0454OC

  • Excel Workbook
  • SOMA assay types: GeneExpressionAssay, GobletCellAssay, FoxJExpressionAssay
  • Key findings: CYP1A1 LFC=6.21 (AhR activation), MUC5AC+ cells FC=2.88, FOXJ1+ nuclei 75% decrease, 424 DEGs at moderate dose

docs.title: Liu et al. (2024)
docs.text:
"PM2.5 Exposure Inhibits Transepithelial Anion Short-circuit Current by Downregulating P2Y2 Receptor/CFTR Pathway"

Int J Med Sci. 2024;21(10):1929-1944 | Paper | DOI: 10.7150/ijms.96777

  • Excel Workbook
  • SOMA assay types: CFTRFunctionAssay, GeneExpressionAssay, GobletCellAssay, BALFSputumAssay, LungFunctionAssay
  • Key findings: PM2.5 downregulates P2Y2R/CFTR (p<0.05), inhibits Isc, increases goblet cells (p<0.001), elevates Th2 cytokines

docs.title: Claude Code Skills for SOMA
docs.text: SOMA includes a set of Claude Code skills that automate the pipeline from publication PDF to validated Excel spreadsheet. This guide explains how to set up Claude Code and use each skill.

docs.title: What Is Claude Code?
docs.text: Claude Code is an AI assistant that lives in your terminal (the text-based command window on your computer). It can read your files, help you write and edit code, plan tasks, and work alongside you on projects. Think of it as a very capable helper that sits inside your coding environment.

docs.title: Important Things to Keep in Mind
docs.text:
Before diving into setup and skills, it is worth understanding what Claude Code is and is not. The following guidance is adapted from Sabrina Toro, PhD and the OBO Academy, based on workshops and bootcamp training for curators and non-developers.

  • Claude is not an oracle. It is an extremely efficient tool, but you should never rely on it alone to tell you how to do something. You need to provide it with context and information so it can help you find the answer.
  • Claude is trained to please you. It will tend to agree with you and show you what you want to see. This means it is not always the best partner for debating ideas or getting pushback. Be aware of this tendency.
  • Stay focused. It is easy to go down a rabbit hole with Claude. Keep your task in mind and avoid scope creep.
  • You must be able to verify the work. Claude cannot do work that you yourself cannot evaluate. If you ask it to extract data from a paper, you need to review the output against the source. If you ask it to suggest ontology terms, you need to confirm they are correct. Claude can suggest approaches you might not have thought of, but ultimately you decide what is right.

docs.title: Getting a Claude Account
docs.text: Claude Code requires a paid plan. It is not available on the free Anthropic tier. The free tier gives you access to claude.ai for basic conversations, but Claude Code (and therefore these skills) require at least a Pro subscription or an API key.

docs.title: Option 1: Claude Pro Plan ($20/month)
docs.text:
1. Go to claude.ai and create an account
  2. Subscribe to the Pro plan ($20/month) under Settings > Subscription
  3. Claude Code is included with Pro

This is the minimum required to use Claude Code and the SOMA skills. Pro gives you 5x the capacity of the free tier and access to all models.

docs.title: Option 2: Claude Max Plan ($100/month, recommended for heavy use)
docs.text:
1. Go to claude.ai and create an account
  2. Subscribe to the Max plan ($100/month) under Settings > Subscription
  3. Claude Code is included with Max -- no API key needed

Max provides significantly higher rate limits (5x Pro), which is useful when running the full PDF-to-Excel pipeline repeatedly. A Max 20x tier is also available at $200/month.

docs.title: Option 3: Anthropic API (recommended for teams or automation)
docs.text:
1. Go to console.anthropic.com and create an Anthropic account
  2. Add a payment method under Settings > Billing
  3. Generate an API key under Settings > API Keys
  4. Set the key in your environment: export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

API billing is pay-per-use and suited for programmatic or team workflows.

docs.title: What if I only have a free account?
docs.text: Claude Code is not available on the free plan. You will need to upgrade to at least the Pro plan ($20/month) to use Claude Code and the SOMA skills. You can sign up for free at claude.ai and upgrade at any time from Settings > Subscription.

docs.title: Installing Claude Code
docs.text:
Install Claude Code globally via npm:

npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

Then launch Claude Code from the SOMA project root:

cd /path/to/soma
claude

If you are on the Max plan, Claude Code will open a browser window to authenticate on first launch. If you are using an API key, make sure ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set in your shell environment before running claude.

The skills are defined in .claude/skills/ and are automatically available when Claude Code runs inside the SOMA repository.

docs.title: The Skills
docs.text:
SOMA provides four skills that form a pipeline:

PDF --> /pdf-to-yaml --> /linkml-validate --> /yaml-to-excel
                              ^
                         /oaklib (ontology lookup)

docs.title: /oaklib - Ontology Term Lookup
docs.text:
Look up, search, and validate ontology terms (CURIEs) used in SOMA data files.

Example usage:

/oaklib
> Look up CHEBI:74481
> Search the Cell Ontology for "nasal epithelial cell"
> Validate that CL:0002603 is a real term

Supported ontologies: CHEBI, CL, UBERON, NCBITaxon, UO, OBI, GO, ECTO, PR, HP, PATO, CLO

Output: Term labels, definitions, ancestors, and cross-references printed directly in the chat.

docs.title: /pdf-to-yaml - Extract Data from a Publication
docs.text:
Reads a publication PDF and extracts structured assay/measurement data into a SOMA-compliant YAML file.

Example usage:

/pdf-to-yaml
> Extract data from docs/papers/smith2024-pm25-ciliary.pdf

What it does:

  1. Reads the PDF (in 20-page chunks)
  2. Identifies assay types, measurements, protocols, and exposure conditions
  3. Maps entities to ontology terms (using /oaklib internally)
  4. Generates a Container YAML file following SOMA naming conventions

Output location: tests/data/valid/Container-<author><year>-<agent>-<focus>.yaml

Important constraints:

  • All numeric values must come from the paper (never hallucinated)
  • Figure-derived values are marked as approximate
  • Missing data is omitted, not guessed

docs.title: /linkml-validate - Validate YAML Against the Schema
docs.text:
Validates a SOMA YAML file against the LinkML schema to catch structural and type errors.

Example usage:

/linkml-validate
> Validate tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml

What it does:

  1. Runs linkml-validate CLI for a quick syntax/structure check
  2. Optionally runs the Python loader for deeper validation
  3. Reports any errors (missing fields, invalid enums, type mismatches)

Output: Validation results printed in the chat. No files are created -- errors are reported for you to fix.

docs.title: /yaml-to-excel - Convert YAML to Excel
docs.text:
Converts a validated SOMA YAML file into a formatted Excel workbook.

Example usage:

/yaml-to-excel
> Convert tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml to Excel

What it does:

  1. Loads and validates the YAML
  2. Reads the LinkML scaffold (project/excel/soma.xlsx) for canonical tab names
  3. Creates tabs for each non-empty collection (Metadata, Protocol, ExposureCondition, KeyEvent, assay tabs, output tabs, etc.)
  4. Applies SOMA styling (blue headers, borders, auto-width columns)

Output location: src/docs/<Author><Year>_<Agent>_<Focus>_SOMA.xlsx

For example:

  • src/docs/Liu2024_PM25_CFTR_SOMA.xlsx
  • src/docs/Montgomery2020_PM25_Mucociliary_SOMA.xlsx

docs.title: Full Pipeline Example
docs.text:
Here is a typical workflow using all four skills in sequence:

> /pdf-to-yaml
  Extract data from docs/papers/liu2024-pm25-cftr.pdf

> /oaklib
  Verify that CHEBI:74481 is correct for PM2.5

> /linkml-validate
  Validate tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml

> /yaml-to-excel
  Convert tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml to Excel

The final Excel file will appear in src/docs/ and can be downloaded from the Artifacts page.

docs.title: Alternative: OpenCode (Open Source)
docs.text:
OpenCode is an open source terminal-based AI coding agent that supports Anthropic Claude models (among many others). It can serve as an alternative to Claude Code if you prefer an open source tool or want to use your own API key without a Pro/Max subscription.

OpenCode does not support Claude Code skills (the /oaklib, /pdf-to-yaml, etc. commands above) directly, but you can use it as a general-purpose AI coding assistant within the SOMA repository using Claude models.

docs.title: Installing OpenCode
docs.text:
macOS (Homebrew):

brew install opencode-ai/tap/opencode

Linux/macOS (install script):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencode-ai/opencode/refs/heads/main/install | bash

Go:

go install github.com/opencode-ai/opencode@latest

docs.title: Connecting to Anthropic
docs.text:
You will need an Anthropic API key. Create one at console.anthropic.com under Settings > API Keys (requires a payment method for pay-per-use billing).

Option A: Interactive setup

Launch OpenCode and use the built-in connection wizard:

cd /path/to/soma
opencode

Inside the TUI, type /connect and select Anthropic. You can authenticate by entering your API key directly.

Option B: Configuration file

Create ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json (global) or opencode.json in the SOMA project root (project-level):

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "provider": {
    "anthropic": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "{env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  },
  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
  "small_model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5"
}

Then set your API key in your shell profile (e.g., ~/.zshrc):

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

docs.title: Enabling Extended Thinking
docs.text:
Claude models in OpenCode support extended thinking for deeper reasoning on complex tasks. Add a models block to your provider config:

{
  "provider": {
    "anthropic": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "{env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}"
      },
      "models": {
        "claude-sonnet-4-5": {
          "options": {
            "thinking": {
              "type": "enabled",
              "budgetTokens": 16000
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5"
}

docs.title: Running OpenCode in the SOMA Repo
docs.text:
cd /path/to/soma
opencode

Once in the TUI, you can ask it to run the same underlying commands that the Claude Code skills use:

> Run: uv run linkml-validate -s src/soma/schema/soma.yaml tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml
> Run: uv run runoak -i sqlite:obo:chebi info CHEBI:74481
> Run: uv run python scripts/yaml_to_excel.py --input tests/data/valid/Container-liu2024-pm25-cftr.yaml --output src/docs/output.xlsx

You can also run a single prompt non-interactively:

opencode -p "Validate all YAML files in tests/data/valid/ against the SOMA schema"

docs.title: Limitations vs Claude Code
docs.text:
• No skills support: OpenCode does not load .claude/skills/ files. You need to provide instructions manually or use OpenCode's own agent configuration to replicate similar behavior.
  • Pay-per-use only: There is no bundled subscription -- you pay Anthropic directly for API usage.
  • Different tool permissions model: OpenCode has its own permission system for file writes, shell commands, etc.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: This page provides comprehensive examples of using the SOMA. All examples use the Container class as the root element and demonstrate real-world use cases for environmental health research data.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
The simplest way to get started is to pick an example that matches your assay type and adapt it to your data. Each example shows:

  • Required fields for the assay type
  • Named measurement slots inside has_specified_output (e.g., beat_frequency_hz, not generic observation_type)
  • Study subject with cell_type on the subject (not the assay) and appropriate detail level
  • Protocols via follows_protocols with protocol_type designator (ImagingProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol, etc.)
  • Exposure conditions via has_exposure_condition (agent, concentration, duration, timing)

docs.text:

docs.title: In Vitro Assays
docs.text: These examples demonstrate assays performed on cell culture systems. The study_subject slot captures the biological model (including cell_type), and follows_protocols captures domain-specific protocol details.

docs.title: Ciliary Function Assay
docs.text:
Measuring ciliary beat frequency (CBF) in primary human bronchial epithelial cells. This assay supports both in vitro and in vivo contexts (supported_contexts: in_vitro_or_in_vivo).

ciliary_function_assays:
  # Example 1: In vitro context using ALI culture
  - id: "CILIARY:001"
    name: "CBF measurement after ozone exposure (in vitro)"
    has_specified_output:
      id: "CILIARY:001-output"
      name: "CILIARY:001 measurement results"
      beat_frequency_hz:
        value: "8.5"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000106"
          name: "hertz"
      active_area_percentage:
        value: "72"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000187"
          name: "percent"
      percentage_ciliated_cells:
        value: "65"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000187"
          name: "percent"
      cilia_length:
        value: "7.2"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000017"
          name: "micrometer"
      cilia_per_cell:
        value: "150"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000189"
          name: "count"
      ciliary_motion_patterns: coordinated
      ciliary_beat_amplitude:
        value: "4.5"
        unit:
          id: "UO:0000017"
          name: "micrometer"
    assay_date: "2024-01-15"
    informs_on_key_event:
      id: "KE:ke3-impaired-ciliary"
      name: "Decreased ciliary function"
      biological_action: decreased
      level_of_biological_organization: cellular
    has_exposure_condition:

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
The schema supports detailed documentation of experimental procedures through typed Protocols (specific procedures).

Key protocol features:

  • protocol_type (on Protocol): designates which concrete Protocol subclass is instantiated (e.g., ImagingProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol). This enables polymorphic dispatch — when protocols are referenced via follows_protocols or sub_protocols, the protocol_type field tells the system which subclass to use for validation and deserialization.
  • follows_protocols (on Assay): multivalued — an assay can reference multiple protocols
  • sub_protocols (on Protocol): protocols can compose other protocols to represent composite workflows (e.g., sample prep, wash steps, post-processing)
  • equipment_required (on Protocol): list of equipment needed for the protocol
  • Any Protocol subclass (ImagingProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol) is valid wherever Protocol is expected

docs.title: Protocol Definition (Base) with Sub-Protocols
docs.text:
A protocol using base Protocol slots, including sub_protocols to compose reusable workflow steps:

protocols:
  - id: "PROTOCOL:001"
    name: "High-speed video microscopy for CBF"
    description: "Protocol for measuring ciliary beat frequency using high-speed video microscopy"
    protocol_version: "2.1"
    quality_control_criteria: "Minimum 5 fields per insert, discard if >50% debris"
    replicate_requirements: 3
    sub_protocols:
      - id: "PROTOCOL:001a"
        name: "Sample preparation for CBF imaging"
        description: "Pre-imaging wash and equilibration steps"
        protocol_version: "1.0"
      - id: "PROTOCOL:001b"
        name: "Post-imaging data export"
        description: "Steps for exporting and archiving video files after acquisition"
        protocol_version: "1.0"

Key points:

  • sub_protocols allows a protocol to reference other protocols as part of its workflow
  • Sub-protocols can be any Protocol subclass (e.g., an ImagingProtocol can include a StainingProtocol as a preparation step)
  • This enables reuse of common steps (wash protocols, fixation, equilibration) across multiple parent protocols

See Container-protocol.yaml for the full data file.

docs.title: Protocols on Assays via follows_protocols

docs.title: Comprehensive AOP Example: PM2.5 Exposure -> Impaired Lung Function
docs.text:
This comprehensive example demonstrates an Adverse Outcome Pathway (AOP) for particulate matter (PM2.5) exposure leading to impaired lung function. The pathway includes:

  • MIE (Molecular Initiating Event): Oxidative stress
  • KE1 (Key Event 1): EGFR activation/phosphorylation
  • KE2 (Key Event 2): Goblet cell hyperplasia and mucin hypersecretion
  • KE3 (Key Event 3): Impaired mucociliary clearance
  • AO (Adverse Outcome): Reduced lung function

Study Design:

  • In vitro: Primary human bronchial epithelial (HBE) cells at ALI
  • In vivo: Clinical cohort with spirometry
  • Exposure: PM2.5 (10 ug/cm2) vs. clean air control
  • Timepoints: 4h (early), 24h (intermediate), 7d (late)

See Container-comprehensive_aop_lung.yaml for the full data file.

Key features demonstrated in the comprehensive example:

  • AOP linkage: Each assay uses informs_on_key_event to connect to the biological pathway
  • Output classes: Measurements wrapped in has_specified_output using domain-specific output classes (e.g., OxidativeStressOutput, CiliaryFunctionOutput, LungFunctionOutput)
  • Named measurement slots: reactive_oxygen_species, egfr_phosphorylation_y1068, beat_frequency_hz, fev1 inside their output classes
  • Protocols via follows_protocols with protocol_type designator: ImagingProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol
  • In vitro study subjects: cell_type on the StudySubject (CellularSystem) for cell culture assays
  • In vivo study subjects: InVivoSubject with age, sex, subject_characteristics for clinical assays
  • Exposure conditions: has_exposure_condition with agent, concentration, duration, and timing_post_exposure
  • Co-exposures: Multivalued has_exposure_condition for PM2.5 + ozone co-exposure
  • Time-course data: Multiple timepoints per assay type showing dose-response

docs.title: SOMA Schema
docs.text:
A LinkML data model for representing biological assays, measurements, and experimental protocols in the context of outcomes research. The schema is centered around ASSAYS that inform on Key Events in Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs), with named slots for specific measurements. This is the main entry point that imports the AOP framework, assay base schema, and domain-specific assay microschemas.

URI: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma

Name: soma

docs.title: Class: AdverseOutcome
docs.text: A specialized type of Key Event that represents the apical endpoint of an Adverse Outcome Pathway. The outcome may be defined at the individual or population level, and is relevant to biomedical, clinical, regulatory, or ecological applications. Because an adverse outcome is itself a Key Event, it inherits upstream_key_events: starting from an outcome, the upstream Key Events can be walked to find every assay that informs them (via each assay's informs_on_key_event), answering "what data is relevant to this outcome?" without requiring a curated AOP record.

docs.title: Class: AssayOutputMeasurement
docs.text:
The measurement results produced by an assay. The specified output of a planned process. Each domain-specific assay class has a corresponding AssayOutputMeasurement subclass containing the named measurement slots for that assay type. This class represents the "output" in the Input/Process/Output model: what was measured and what values were obtained.

One AssayOutputMeasurement record represents the results for ONE experimental condition or group. When a study reports a control group and one or more treated groups (or a dose-response series), each group gets its own output record, marked with experimental_group and linked to the specific exposure condition via measured_under.

When a paper reports a result only as a chart or image (a bar graph, a stained section) and no exact number appears in the text, still create the output record: set data_in_figure_only, leave the numeric measurement slots empty, and attach an evidence item whose figure_reference names the figure, so the endpoint and its location are captured even though the value is not.

docs.title: Class: CiliaryFunctionAssay
docs.text:
Assay for measuring ciliary function including beat frequency, active area, cilia morphology, and ciliated cell populations. Informs on Key Event: "Decreased ciliary function" in respiratory AOPs.

CONTEXT: Can be performed in vitro (tissue slices, spheroids) or in vivo (often using optical coherence tomography).

TIER 1 slots (critical): beat_frequency_hz, active_area_percentage, cilia_length, cilia_per_cell, percentage_ciliated_cells, cell_type_ratios,

docs.text:
Root container for outcomes research data. Organized around ASSAYS that inform on Key Events in Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs).

The schema is assay-centric: each assay class contains named slots for its specific measurements, with an explicit connection to the Key Event it informs via the informs_on_key_event slot.

docs.title: Class: EvidenceItem
docs.text:
One piece of evidence for a claim: which publication it comes from, an exact quote from that publication, whether the quote supports or refutes the claim, and what kind of study produced it.

It also records where in the paper the supporting data sits: article_section says which section the quote was taken from (a dose quoted from Methods storage boilerplate is much weaker provenance than one quoted from Results), and figure_reference names the figure or table that reports the underlying data, so a reviewer can find values the extraction could not read out of a chart or image.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: EvidenceItem
description: 'One piece of evidence for a claim: which publication it comes from,
  an exact quote from that publication, whether the quote supports or refutes the
  claim, and what kind of study produced it.

  It also records where in the paper the supporting data sits: article_section says
  which section the quote was taken from (a dose quoted from Methods storage boilerplate
  is much weaker provenance than one quoted from Results), and figure_reference names
  the figure or table that reports the underlying data, so a reviewer can find values
  the extraction could not read out of a chart or image.'
from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
attributes:
  reference:
    name: reference
    implements:
    - linkml:authoritative_reference
    description: The cited publication's PubMed ID, e.g. "PMID:12345678".
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    - PublicationReference
    range: PMID
    pattern: ^PMID:\d+$
  reference_title:
    name: reference_title
    implements:
    - dcterms:title
    description: The title of the cited publication, copied from the cached reference
      record (references_cache/), never typed from memory.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    - PublicationReference
    range: string
    recommended: true
  supports:
    name: supports
    description: 'Which way the quoted evidence points: does it support the claim,
      contradict it, or turn out not to bear on it at all.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: EvidenceItemSupportEnum
  evidence_source:
    name: evidence_source
    description: What kind of study the cited publication reports — classify the paper,
      not the person doing the extraction.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: EvidenceSourceEnum
  snippet:
    name: snippet
    implements:
    - linkml:excerpt
    description: 'An exact quote from the cited publication that supports or refutes
      the claim. Checked automatically: the text must appear word-for-word in the
      cached copy of the publication.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: string
  explanation:
    name: explanation
    description: One or two sentences on how the quoted passage supports the specific
      claim it is attached to.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: string
  article_section:
    name: article_section
    description: 'The section of the publication the quoted passage comes from (abstract,
      methods, results, a figure caption, a table, ...). Recording the section makes
      provenance reviewable: a dose or response value quoted from Results carries
      more weight than one quoted from a Methods sentence about how a compound was
      stored.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: ArticleSectionEnum
  figure_reference:
    name: figure_reference
    description: The figure or table in the publication that reports the data behind
      this claim, written the way the paper labels it, e.g. "Figure 10", "Figure 3B",
      "Table 2". Use this whenever the quantitative result lives in a figure or chart
      — even when no exact value could be read from it — so a reviewer knows exactly
      where to look.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: EvidenceItem
    domain_of:
    - EvidenceItem
    range: string

Key events can be Molecular Initiating Events (MIEs), intermediate Key Events, or Adverse Outcomes at the organism/population level.

docs.title: Class: LungFunctionAssay
docs.text:
Clinical assay for measuring lung function. Informs on Adverse Outcome: "Decreased lung function" - the composite clinical outcome.

IMPORTANT per domain feedback: - Subject characteristics (sex, species, age, height) are critical -

_ often reported as % of predicted baseline_

- Reference dataset (GLI-2012 for humans) is essential for interpretation - Hemoglobin levels pair with DLCO measurements - Recent respiratory illness affects spirometry results

TIER 1 slots (critical): fev1, fvc, subject_characteristics, reference_dataset. This assay is IN VIVO ONLY.

docs.title: Induced

  \  often reported as % of predicted baseline\n- Reference dataset (GLI-2012 for\

      exact quote from a cited publication.

    domain_of:
    - KeyEvent
    - KeyEventRelationship
    - Assay
    - AssayOutputMeasurement
    range: EvidenceItem
    recommended: true
    multivalued: true
    inlined: true
    inlined_as_list: true
  experimental_group:
    name: experimental_group
    description: 'The role of this output record''s group in the experimental design:
      control, vehicle control, baseline, treated, recovery, or sham. Lets extraction
      distinguish the control/baseline response from the treated response so a change
      relative to control can be assembled downstream.'
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: LungFunctionOutput
    domain_of:
    - AssayOutputMeasurement
    range: ExperimentalGroupEnum
  measured_under:
    name: measured_under
    description: Reference (by id) to the specific ExposureCondition this output record
      was measured under. Links each set of response values to the concentration/treatment
      it corresponds to, so a dose-response series keeps each response paired with
      its exposure level. The referenced condition should be listed in the assay's
      has_exposure_condition.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: LungFunctionOutput
    domain_of:
    - AssayOutputMeasurement
    range: ExposureCondition
    inlined: false
  data_in_figure_only:
    name: data_in_figure_only
    description: True when the quantitative values for this output record are reported
      only in a figure or chart and could not be read from the text. The record then
      documents that the endpoint was measured and where its data lives (via an evidence
      item's figure_reference and article_section), without numeric values. This keeps
      figure-only results visible to reviewers in the workbook instead of silently
      dropping them.
    from_schema: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma
    rank: 1000
    owner: LungFunctionOutput
    domain_of:
    - AssayOutputMeasurement
    range: boolean

    owner: LungFunctionOutput

docs.title: Class: ResponseComparison
docs.text: An analysis-layer record describing the change in a measured response between a control/baseline group and a treated group. Lives alongside the extracted assay data rather than inside it: papers report changes in many forms (absolute difference, percent change, fold change, ratio), and downstream models need a single change value with an uncertainty measure. References the control and treated output records by id, names the measurement being compared, and states the kind, direction, and size of the change. Use derivation to record whether the change was reported in the paper or computed afterwards.

    range: string

docs.title: Class: Variability
docs.text: The reported spread or uncertainty around a measured value, kept separate from the value itself because papers report it in different forms. Use variability_type to say what was reported (standard deviation, standard error, confidence interval, range) and either a single magnitude (value) or bounds (lower_bound/upper_bound), with a unit when it differs from the measurement's unit.

docs.title: Induced

name: Variability
description: The reported spread or uncertainty around a measured value, kept separate

  to say what was reported (standard deviation, standard error, confidence interval,
  range) and either a single magnitude (value) or bounds (lower_bound/upper_bound),
  with a unit when it differs from the measurement's unit.

docs.title: Enum: VariabilityTypeEnum
docs.text: Kinds of variability or uncertainty reported around a value.

docs.title: Slot: active_area_percentage
docs.text: Percentage of epithelial surface with actively beating cilia. TIER 1 - critical for assessing ciliary coverage.

docs.title: Slot: adverse_outcome
docs.text: The adverse outcome that is the apical endpoint of this AOP.

docs.title: Slot: adverse_outcome_pathways
docs.text: Collection of Adverse Outcome Pathways. AOPs describe sequences of causally linked events from molecular initiating events to adverse outcomes.

docs.title: Slot: adverse_outcomes
docs.text: Adverse outcomes described in this container. Listing outcomes at the container level makes them a first-class entry point: each outcome names its upstream Key Events, and assays reference those Key Events via informs_on_key_event, closing the Outcome - Key Event - Assay traversal in both directions.

docs.title: Slot: age
docs.text: Age of the subject.

docs.title: Slot: age_range
docs.text: Age range of the study population.

docs.title: Slot: airway_region
docs.text: Region of airway from which cells originated.

docs.title: Slot: akt_phosphorylation
docs.text: AKT phosphorylation level. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: alpha_diversity
docs.text: Alpha diversity (microbiome).

docs.title: Slot: analysis_software
docs.text: Software used for analysis (e.g., SAVA, Cilia FA).

docs.title: Slot: antibodies_used
docs.text: Antibodies used in staining or detection.

docs.title: Slot: antioxidant_capacity
docs.text: Total antioxidant capacity or GSH/GSSG ratio. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: antioxidant_enzyme_activities
docs.text: Antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, catalase, GPx). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: aopwiki_id
docs.text: The AOP-Wiki identifier for this entity (e.g., "AOP:411" for an AOP, "KE:1234" for a key event).

docs.title: Slot: article_section
docs.text: The section of the publication the quoted passage comes from (abstract, methods, results, a figure caption, a table, ...). Recording the section makes provenance reviewable: a dose or response value quoted from Results carries more weight than one quoted from a Methods sentence about how a compound was stored.

docs.title: Slot: asl_assays
docs.text: Collection of airway surface liquid assays. Informs on Key Event: "Decreased ASL height" or "Altered airway hydration".

docs.title: Slot: asl_height_um
docs.text: Airway surface liquid height in micrometers. TIER 1 - primary measurement for ASL assays.

docs.title: Slot: asl_ph
docs.text: pH of airway surface liquid. TIER 3.

docs.title: Slot: assay_date
docs.text: Date when the assay was performed.

docs.title: Slot: bacterial_load
docs.text: Bacterial load (16S copies or CFU).

docs.title: Slot: balf_sputum_assays
docs.text: Collection of BALF and sputum assays. In vivo only. Informs on Key Event: "Airway inflammation".

docs.title: Slot: beat_frequency_hz
docs.text: Ciliary beat frequency measured in Hz. TIER 1 - critical for assessing ciliary function.

docs.title: Slot: beta_diversity
docs.text: Beta diversity (microbiome).

docs.title: Slot: biological_action
docs.text: The type of change (increased, decreased, altered, impaired).

docs.title: Slot: biological_object
docs.text: The biological entity affected (protein, cell, tissue, organ).

docs.title: Slot: biological_process
docs.text: The biological process affected by this key event. Should reference a GO biological process term.

docs.title: Slot: bronchodilator_agent
docs.text: Bronchodilator agent used (e.g., albuterol).

docs.title: Slot: bronchodilator_dose
docs.text: Dose of bronchodilator administered.

docs.title: Slot: bronchodilator_response
docs.text: Response to bronchodilator (% change in FEV1). TIER 2 - informs reversibility.

docs.title: Slot: catalase_activity
docs.text: Catalase activity. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: cell_free_dna
docs.text: Cell-free DNA concentration.

docs.title: Slot: cell_type
docs.text: The cell type being studied. Reference to a Cell Ontology (CL) term. Used on CellularSystem and CellLine to describe the cell identity.

docs.title: Slot: central_tendency
docs.text: What kind of central value the reported number is: a mean, median, geometric mean, or a single measurement. Important for combining results across studies.

docs.title: Slot: cftr_assays
docs.text: Collection of CFTR function assays. Informs on Key Event: "Decreased CFTR function".

docs.title: Slot: cftr_chloride_secretion
docs.text: CFTR-mediated chloride secretion in uA/cm2.

docs.title: Slot: cftr_forskolin_response
docs.text: Forskolin-stimulated CFTR response.

docs.title: Slot: cftr_specific_current
docs.text: CFTR-specific chloride secretory current.

docs.title: Slot: change_direction
docs.text: Direction of the change in the treated group relative to control.

docs.title: Slot: change_type
docs.text: How the change is expressed: an absolute difference, a percent change, a fold change, or a ratio. Papers report changes in different forms; this makes the form explicit so values can be compared or converted downstream.

docs.title: Slot: change_value
docs.text: The size of the change, with its unit and (when reported) its uncertainty. For a percent change the unit is percent; for an absolute difference it is the measurement's unit; fold changes and ratios are dimensionless.

docs.title: Slot: cilia_length
docs.text: Length of cilia measured in micrometers. TIER 1 - morphological assessment of cilia.

docs.title: Slot: cilia_per_cell
docs.text: Number of cilia per ciliated cell. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: ciliary_beat_amplitude
docs.text: Amplitude of ciliary beat. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: ciliary_function_assays
docs.text: Collection of ciliary function assays. Informs on Key Event: "Decreased ciliary function". Contains named slots for beat frequency, active area, cilia length, etc.

docs.title: Slot: ciliary_motion_patterns
docs.text: Patterns of ciliary motion (coordinated, dyskinetic, immotile). TIER 2 - supporting information.

docs.title: Slot: clinical_context
docs.text: Clinical context for in vivo measurements (e.g., routine screening, post-exposure assessment, disease monitoring, baseline spirometry).

docs.title: Slot: cohort_size
docs.text: Number of subjects in the cohort or population.

docs.title: Slot: collection_date
docs.text: Date when the sample was collected.

docs.title: Slot: collection_site
docs.text: Anatomical site of sample collection.

docs.title: Slot: compared_measurement
docs.text: The name of the measurement slot being compared (e.g., "total_lung_capacity", "beat_frequency_hz"), matching the slot name in the referenced output records.

docs.title: Slot: control_output
docs.text: Reference (by id) to the AssayOutputMeasurement record for the control or baseline group.

docs.title: Slot: counterstain
docs.text: Counterstain used (e.g., hematoxylin, DAPI).

docs.title: Slot: data_in_figure_only
docs.text: True when the quantitative values for this output record are reported only in a figure or chart and could not be read from the text. The record then documents that the endpoint was measured and where its data lives (via an evidence item's figure_reference and article_section), without numeric values. This keeps figure-only results visible to reviewers in the workbook instead of silently dropping them.

docs.title: Slot: days_at_differentiation
docs.text: Days at air-liquid interface or differentiation stage.

docs.title: Slot: decline_rate
docs.text: Longitudinal decline rate in mL/year. TIER 2 - useful for pre/post comparisons.

docs.title: Slot: derivation
docs.text: Whether this change was reported directly in the paper or computed afterwards from the extracted control and treated values.

docs.title: Slot: derived_from_assay
docs.text: Reference (by id) to the assay whose output records this comparison is derived from.

docs.title: Slot: description
docs.text: A detailed description of the entity.

docs.title: Slot: detection_method
docs.text: Detection method used (e.g., flow cytometry, plate reader).

docs.title: Slot: detection_method_details
docs.text: Detection method details. TIER 1 per feedback - expected to have multiple detection methods.

docs.title: Slot: dlco
docs.text: Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide. TIER 2 - measure of fibrosis, needs hemoglobin level.

docs.title: Slot: dna_damage_markers
docs.text: DNA damage markers (8-OHdG). TIER 1 - surrogate for OS.

docs.title: Slot: doi
docs.text: The publication's DOI, e.g. "10.1164/rccm.202001-0086OC" (without a "DOI:" prefix).

docs.title: Slot: donor_info
docs.text: Information about cell donor (e.g., healthy non-smoker, CF patient, age, anatomical region).

docs.title: Slot: downstream_event
docs.text: The downstream key event in this relationship (effect).

docs.title: Slot: downstream_key_events
docs.text: Key events that follow this key event (downstream in the pathway).

docs.title: Slot: downstream_kinase_activation
docs.text: Activation levels of downstream kinases. TIER 2 - not specific to EGFR alone without phosphorylation data.

docs.title: Slot: egfr_ligand_expression
docs.text: Expression of EGFR ligands (EGF, TGF-alpha, amphiregulin).

docs.title: Slot: egfr_membrane_localization
docs.text: EGFR membrane localization percentage.

docs.title: Slot: egfr_phosphorylation_y1068
docs.text: EGFR phosphorylation at Y1068 residue (fold change). TIER 1 - MOST SPECIFIC evidence for EGFR activation.

docs.title: Slot: egfr_phosphorylation_y1173
docs.text: EGFR phosphorylation at Y1173 residue (fold change). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: egfr_signaling_assays
docs.text: Collection of EGFR signaling assays. Informs on Key Event: "EGFR activation". Note: EGFR phosphorylation is the most specific evidence for activation.

docs.title: Slot: eight_isoprostane_level
docs.text: 8-isoprostane level.

docs.title: Slot: eight_ohdg_level
docs.text: 8-OHdG level (DNA oxidation marker). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: eosinophil_percentage
docs.text: Eosinophil percentage in BALF/sputum.

docs.title: Slot: equipment_required
docs.text: Equipment required for this protocol.

docs.title: Slot: erk_phosphorylation
docs.text: ERK phosphorylation level. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: evaporation_prevention
docs.text: Method used to prevent evaporation (e.g., perfluorocarbon overlay).

docs.title: Slot: evidence
docs.text: Evidence items backing this object's claims. Each one carries an exact quote from a cited publication.

docs.title: Slot: evidence_source
docs.text: What kind of study the cited publication reports — classify the paper, not the person doing the extraction.

docs.title: Slot: evidence_support
docs.text: Level of evidence supporting this key event relationship.

docs.title: Slot: experimental_group
docs.text: The role of this output record's group in the experimental design: control, vehicle control, baseline, treated, recovery, or sham. Lets extraction distinguish the control/baseline response from the treated response so a change relative to control can be assembled downstream.

docs.title: Slot: explanation
docs.text: One or two sentences on how the quoted passage supports the specific claim it is attached to.

docs.title: Slot: exposure_agent
docs.text: The chemical, biological, or environmental agent used for exposure or treatment. Reference to a CHEBI or ECTO ontology term.

docs.title: Slot: exposure_concentration
docs.text: Concentration of the exposure agent applied.

docs.title: Slot: exposure_duration
docs.text: Duration of exposure or treatment.

docs.title: Slot: fef25_75
docs.text: Forced expiratory flow 25-75%. TIER 3 - more variable than FEV1, FVC.

docs.title: Slot: feno
docs.text: Fractional exhaled nitric oxide in ppb. TIER 2 - marker for airway inflammation.

docs.title: Slot: fev1
docs.text: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second. TIER 1 - primary spirometry measurement.

docs.title: Slot: fev1_fvc_ratio
docs.text: Ratio of FEV1 to FVC (Tiffeneau-Pinelli index). TIER 2 - can be calculated from FEV1 and FVC.

docs.title: Slot: figure_reference
docs.text: The figure or table in the publication that reports the data behind this claim, written the way the paper labels it, e.g. "Figure 10", "Figure 3B", "Table 2". Use this whenever the quantitative result lives in a figure or chart — even when no exact value could be read from it — so a reviewer knows exactly where to look.

docs.title: Slot: fixation_method
docs.text: Fixation method used for tissue/cell preparation.

docs.title: Slot: fluorescent_labeling
docs.text: Fluorescent label or tracer used.

docs.title: Slot: fluorescent_tracer
docs.text: Fluorescent tracer used for tracking (MCC assays).

docs.title: Slot: follows_protocols
docs.text: The Protocol(s) that this assay follows. Any Protocol or Protocol subclass (ImagingProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol) is valid. Use this for general protocol references; assay subclasses also have typed protocol slots for domain-specific protocols.

docs.title: Slot: four_hydroxynonenal_level
docs.text: 4-HNE level - lipid peroxidation marker.

docs.title: Slot: foxj1_mrna_expression
docs.text: FoxJ1 mRNA expression level.

docs.title: Slot: foxj1_nuclear_localization
docs.text: FoxJ1 nuclear localization.

docs.title: Slot: foxj1_positive_cell_percentage
docs.text: Percentage of FoxJ1-positive cells.

docs.title: Slot: foxj1_protein_expression
docs.text: FoxJ1 protein expression level.

docs.title: Slot: foxj_assays
docs.text: Collection of FoxJ1/ciliogenesis assays. Informs on Key Event: "Altered ciliogenesis".

docs.title: Slot: functional_residual_capacity
docs.text: Functional residual capacity. TIER 3 - requires more equipment.

docs.title: Slot: fvc
docs.text: Forced vital capacity. TIER 1 - primary spirometry measurement.

docs.title: Slot: gene_expression_assays
docs.text: Collection of gene expression assays. Generic assay for gene/protein expression measurements.

docs.title: Slot: gene_expression_method
docs.text: Method used for gene expression (qRT-PCR, RNA-seq, etc.).

docs.title: Slot: general_procedure
docs.text: High-level description of the procedure.

docs.title: Slot: glutathione_peroxidase_activity
docs.text: GPx activity. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: glutathione_ratio
docs.text: GSH/GSSG ratio indicating antioxidant status. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: goblet_cell_assays
docs.text: Collection of goblet cell and mucin assays. Informs on Key Event: "Goblet cell hyperplasia" or "Mucin hypersecretion". Combined from previous GobletCellMeasurement and MucinProductionMeasurement.

docs.title: Slot: goblet_cell_count
docs.text: Number of goblet cells (raw count). TIER 1 - want both raw and relative information.

docs.title: Slot: goblet_cell_percentage
docs.text: Percentage of goblet cells. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: goblet_to_ciliated_ratio
docs.text: Ratio of goblet cells to ciliated cells. TIER 2 - related to transdifferentiation but not critical for outcome.

docs.title: Slot: has_exposure_condition
docs.text: The exposure condition(s) applied to the study subject. Captures the agent, concentration, duration, and timing of exposure/treatment. Multivalued to support co-exposures or dose-response series.

docs.title: Slot: has_specified_output
docs.text: The measurement results produced by this assay — the specified output of a planned process (OBI). Contains the domain-specific measurement values (e.g., beat frequency, cilia length for CiliaryFunctionAssay). Multivalued: one output record per experimental condition or group, so a control group and each treatment concentration in a dose-response series each get their own record (marked with experimental_group and linked to the exposure via measured_under).

docs.title: Slot: hemoglobin_level
docs.text: Hemoglobin level. TIER 2 - pairs with DLCO.

docs.title: Slot: humidity_control
docs.text: Humidity conditions during the procedure.

docs.title: Slot: id
docs.text: A unique identifier for the entity.

docs.title: Slot: il1_beta_concentration
docs.text: IL-1 beta concentration.

docs.title: Slot: il6_concentration
docs.text: IL-6 concentration.

docs.title: Slot: il8_concentration
docs.text: IL-8 concentration.

docs.title: Slot: imaging_duration
docs.text: Duration of imaging session.

docs.title: Slot: imaging_frame_rate
docs.text: Frame rate for video/imaging acquisition (e.g., 200 fps).

docs.title: Slot: imaging_protocol
docs.text: Reference to the imaging protocol used. TIER 1 for CBF, ASL assays.

docs.title: Slot: inclusion_criteria
docs.text: Criteria for inclusion in the study population.

docs.title: Slot: informs_on_key_event
docs.text: The Key Event that this assay provides evidence for. This establishes the mechanistic connection between the assay measurements and the Adverse Outcome Pathway framework. Multiple assays can inform on the same key event, providing converging evidence.

docs.title: Slot: inhibitor_sensitive_current
docs.text: Inhibitor-sensitive current measurement.

docs.title: Slot: inhibitor_used
docs.text: Inhibitor used (e.g., CFTRinh-172).

docs.title: Slot: institution
docs.text: Institution where protocol was developed.

docs.title: Slot: ion_composition
docs.text: Ionic composition (Cl-, Na+, K+). TIER 3 - not critical for comparison but relevant for mechanism.

docs.title: Slot: key_event_relationships
docs.text: The key event relationships connecting events in this AOP.

docs.title: Slot: key_events
docs.text: The key events in this AOP (intermediate events between MIE and AO).

docs.title: Slot: key_reagents
docs.text: Key reagents needed for this protocol.

docs.title: Slot: last_updated
docs.text: Date protocol was last updated.

docs.title: Slot: level_of_biological_organization
docs.text: The level of biological organization at which this key event occurs.

docs.title: Slot: lipid_peroxidation
docs.text: Lipid peroxidation level. TIER 1 - surrogate marker for OS.

docs.title: Slot: lower_bound
docs.text: Lower bound when variability is reported as an interval (confidence interval, range, IQR).

docs.title: Slot: lung_compliance
docs.text: Lung compliance. TIER 3 - most often reported for animals, difficult to relate to human exposure.

docs.title: Slot: lung_elastance
docs.text: Lung elastance. TIER 3 - most often reported for animals.

docs.title: Slot: lung_function_assays
docs.text: Collection of lung function assays. In vivo only. Informs on Adverse Outcome: "Decreased lung function" - the composite clinical outcome.

docs.title: Slot: lung_resistance
docs.text: Lung resistance. TIER 3 - most often reported for animals.

docs.title: Slot: lymphocyte_percentage
docs.text: Lymphocyte percentage in BALF/sputum.

docs.title: Slot: lysis_buffer
docs.text: Lysis buffer used for sample preparation.

docs.title: Slot: macrophage_percentage
docs.text: Macrophage percentage in BALF/sputum.

docs.title: Slot: malondialdehyde_level
docs.text: MDA level - lipid peroxidation marker.

docs.title: Slot: mcc_assays
docs.text: Collection of mucociliary clearance assays. Informs on Key Event: "Impaired mucociliary clearance".

docs.title: Slot: measured_under
docs.text: Reference (by id) to the specific ExposureCondition this output record was measured under. Links each set of response values to the concentration/treatment it corresponds to, so a dose-response series keeps each response paired with its exposure level. The referenced condition should be listed in the assay's has_exposure_condition.

docs.title: Slot: member_of_cohort
docs.text: The cohort this subject record belongs to. Use when one study cohort is sampled in multiple ways: give each sampling context its own InVivoSubject with its specimen slots, and point them all to one PopulationSubject holding cohort_size and shared characteristics.

docs.title: Slot: molecular_initiating_event
docs.text: The molecular initiating event that starts this AOP.

docs.title: Slot: molecular_protocol
docs.text: Reference to the molecular assay protocol used.

docs.title: Slot: mrna_level
docs.text: mRNA expression level.

docs.title: Slot: muc5ac_mrna_expression
docs.text: MUC5AC mRNA expression level (fold change). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: muc5ac_muc5b_ratio
docs.text: MUC5AC to MUC5B ratio. TIER 1 - important for disease state.

docs.title: Slot: muc5ac_protein_expression
docs.text: MUC5AC protein expression level. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: muc5b_mrna_expression
docs.text: MUC5B mRNA expression level (fold change). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: muc5b_protein_expression
docs.text: MUC5B protein expression level. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: mucin_protein_concentration
docs.text: Total mucin protein concentration. TIER 1 - want both direct and comparative measures.

docs.title: Slot: mucin_secretion_rate
docs.text: Mucin secretion rate. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: mucus_composition
docs.text: Composition of mucus. TIER 2 per feedback.

docs.title: Slot: mucus_layer_thickness
docs.text: Thickness of the mucus gel layer in micrometers. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: mucus_viscosity
docs.text: Mucus viscosity in centipoise. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: name
docs.text: A human-readable name for the entity.

docs.title: Slot: nasal_potential_difference
docs.text: Nasal potential difference in mV.

docs.title: Slot: neutrophil_percentage
docs.text: Neutrophil percentage in BALF/sputum.

docs.title: Slot: nitrotyrosine_level
docs.text: Nitrotyrosine level. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: normalization_method
docs.text: Method used for data normalization.

docs.title: Slot: normalization_reference
docs.text: Normalization reference (beta-actin, GAPDH, total EGFR).

docs.title: Slot: nrf2_activation
docs.text: Nrf2 activation level. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: obi_mapping
docs.text: OBI ontology term for this method.

docs.title: Slot: occurs_in_anatomy
docs.text: The anatomical location where this key event occurs. Should reference a UBERON anatomy term.

docs.title: Slot: occurs_in_cell_type
docs.text: The cell type in which this key event occurs. Should reference a Cell Ontology (CL) term.

docs.title: Slot: outcome_level
docs.text: The level at which the adverse outcome manifests (individual, population).

docs.title: Slot: outcome_term
docs.text: The disease or phenotype this adverse outcome corresponds to, as a MONDO disease term or an HPO phenotype term. Grounding the outcome to an ontology term makes it findable by name across containers: a query can start from the outcome term, walk upstream_key_events, and collect the assays whose informs_on_key_event matches any Key Event in the chain.

docs.title: Slot: oxidative_stress_assays
docs.text: Collection of oxidative stress assays. Informs on Key Event: "Increased oxidative stress" - often a Molecular Initiating Event.

docs.title: Slot: p_value
docs.text: Reported p-value for the comparison, when available.

docs.title: Slot: particle_clearance_time
docs.text: Time for particle clearance. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: particle_size
docs.text: Size of tracking particles.

docs.title: Slot: particle_tracking_method
docs.text: Method used for tracking particles or mucus.

docs.title: Slot: pathway_biomarkers
docs.text: Pathway-specific biomarker signatures. TIER 2 - relationship to outcome needs further investigation.

docs.title: Slot: peak_expiratory_flow
docs.text: Peak expiratory flow. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: percent_solids
docs.text: Percent solids in apical secretion (overall secretion). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: percentage_active_transport
docs.text: Percentage of area showing active transport. TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: percentage_ciliated_cells
docs.text: Percentage of cells that are ciliated. TIER 1 - critical for understanding ciliated cell populations.

docs.title: Slot: percentage_positive_cells
docs.text: Percentage of positive cells (IHC, flow cytometry).

docs.title: Slot: periciliary_layer_depth
docs.text: Depth of the periciliary layer in micrometers. TIER 1 - helps give confidence to the outcome.

docs.title: Slot: phosphorylation_site
docs.text: Specific phosphorylation site being measured.

docs.title: Slot: platform
docs.text: Assay platform or instrument used (e.g., QuantStudio, Illumina).

docs.title: Slot: plethysmography_method
docs.text: Method for plethysmography measurement.

docs.title: Slot: primer_sequences
docs.text: Primer sequences used for PCR-based methods.

docs.title: Slot: protein_carbonyl_content
docs.text: Protein carbonyl content. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: protein_level
docs.text: Protein expression level.

docs.title: Slot: protein_oxidation_markers
docs.text: Protein oxidation markers (carbonyls, nitrotyrosine). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: protocol_author
docs.text: Author of the protocol.

docs.title: Slot: protocol_type
docs.text: The specific type of protocol. Used to designate which concrete class (e.g., ImagingProtocol, StainingProtocol, SpirometryProtocol, MolecularAssayProtocol) is instantiated for polymorphic protocol slots.

docs.title: Slot: protocol_version
docs.text: Version of the protocol.

docs.title: Slot: protocols
docs.text: Collection of protocols. Contains Tier 2/3 procedural details important for reproducibility.

docs.title: Slot: publication_reference
docs.text: Reference to protocol publication.

docs.title: Slot: quality_control_criteria
docs.text: Quality control acceptance criteria.

docs.title: Slot: quantitative_understanding
docs.text: Level of quantitative understanding of the relationship.

docs.title: Slot: reactive_oxygen_species
docs.text: ROS level as fold change or fluorescence intensity. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: recent_respiratory_illness
docs.text: Recent respiratory illness (affects spirometry). TIER 2.

docs.title: Slot: reference
docs.text: The cited publication's PubMed ID, e.g. "PMID:12345678".

docs.title: Slot: reference_dataset
docs.text: Reference dataset for interpretation (GLI-2012 for humans). TIER 1 - essential for interpretation.

docs.title: Slot: reference_gene
docs.text: Reference/housekeeping gene used for normalization.

docs.title: Slot: reference_title
docs.text: The title of the cited publication, copied from the cached reference record (references_cache/), never typed from memory.

docs.title: Slot: relationship_type
docs.text: The type of causal relationship (directly leads to, indirectly leads to).

docs.title: Slot: replicate_requirements
docs.text: Number of replicates required.

docs.title: Slot: replicates_per_donor
docs.text: Number of biological replicates per donor.

docs.title: Slot: residual_volume
docs.text: Residual volume. TIER 3 - requires more equipment.

docs.title: Slot: response_comparisons
docs.text: Collection of analysis-layer records comparing treated responses to control/baseline responses. Kept separate from the extracted assay data: each comparison references the control and treated output records and states the kind, direction, and size of the change with its uncertainty.

docs.title: Slot: ros_probe_type
docs.text: Type of ROS probe used (DCFDA, DHE, MitoSOX, etc.). TIER 1 - varies by method.

docs.title: Slot: sample_collection_method
docs.text: Method used for sample collection in vivo (e.g., bronchoscopy, induced sputum, spirometry).

docs.title: Slot: sample_size
docs.text: Number of subjects, samples, or replicates behind this value.

docs.title: Slot: sample_type
docs.text: Type of biological sample (e.g., sputum, BALF, blood).

docs.title: Slot: sex
docs.text: Biological sex of the subject.

docs.title: Slot: snippet
docs.text: An exact quote from the cited publication that supports or refutes the claim. Checked automatically: the text must appear word-for-word in the cached copy of the publication.

docs.title: soma
docs.text:
A LinkML data model for representing biological assays, measurements, and experimental protocols in the context of outcomes research. The schema is centered around ASSAYS that inform on Key Events in Adverse Outcome Pathways (AOPs), with named slots for specific measurements. This is the main entry point that imports the AOP framework, assay base schema, and domain-specific assay microschemas.

URI: https://w3id.org/EHS-Data-Standards/soma

docs.title: Slot: sop_reference
docs.text: Reference to standard operating procedure document.

docs.title: Slot: source_publication
docs.text: The publication this data was extracted from.

docs.title: Slot: spatial_resolution
docs.text: Spatial resolution of imaging (e.g., 1-2 um axial resolution).

docs.title: Slot: species
docs.text: The species of origin for the cells, organism, or population being studied. Reference to NCBITaxon term. Applies to any study subject: a human cohort records Homo sapiens here just as a cell line records its species of origin.

docs.title: Slot: spirometry_protocol
docs.text: Reference to the spirometry protocol used.

docs.title: Slot: spirometry_standard
docs.text: Spirometry standard followed (e.g., ATS/ERS 2019).

docs.title: Slot: staining_protocol
docs.text: Reference to staining protocol (AB-PAS, immunochem). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: staining_type
docs.text: Type of staining used (e.g., immunofluorescence, AB-PAS).

docs.title: Slot: statistical_test
docs.text: Statistical test used for the comparison (e.g., t-test, ANOVA), when reported.

docs.title: Slot: stimulation_agent
docs.text: Stimulation agent used (e.g., forskolin concentration).

docs.title: Slot: stressors
docs.text: Chemical or physical stressors that can trigger this AOP.

docs.title: Slot: study_subject
docs.text: The subject of the study — what the assay is performed on. Can be a ModelSystem (e.g., CellularSystem), an InVivoSubject, or a PopulationSubject. The type of subject determines which context slots are available.

docs.title: Slot: sub_protocols
docs.text: Other protocols that are part of this protocol's workflow. Use this to compose protocols from reusable steps (e.g., sample preparation, wash steps, fixation, post-processing). Any Protocol or Protocol subclass is valid.

docs.title: Slot: subject_characteristics
docs.text: Relevant subject characteristics (disease state, medications, etc.). TIER 1 for LungFunctionAssay per user feedback.

docs.title: Slot: subject_type
docs.text: The specific type of study subject. Used to designate which concrete class (e.g., CellularSystem, InVivoSubject) is instantiated for polymorphic study_subject slots.

docs.title: Slot: subjects
docs.text: Individual subjects in the population or cohort. Optional — use when individual-level data is available alongside aggregate cohort metadata.

docs.title: Slot: superoxide_dismutase_activity
docs.text: SOD activity. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: supports
docs.text: Which way the quoted evidence points: does it support the claim, contradict it, or turn out not to bear on it at all.

docs.title: Slot: sweat_chloride_concentration
docs.text: Sweat chloride concentration in mEq/L (CF diagnostic).

docs.title: Slot: target_cell_type
docs.text: The specific cell type that is the primary focus of this assay's analysis, when the assay examines multiple cell populations in a sample (e.g., neutrophils in a BALF differential).

docs.title: Slot: target_gene
docs.text: Target gene being measured.

docs.title: Slot: target_molecule
docs.text: The molecular target of the stressor in the MIE (e.g., receptor, enzyme).

docs.title: Slot: temperature_control
docs.text: Temperature conditions during the procedure (e.g., 37C).

docs.title: Slot: timing_post_exposure
docs.text: Time after exposure when the measurement was taken. Used to capture the temporal relationship between exposure and assay readout.

docs.title: Slot: tnf_alpha_concentration
docs.text: TNF-alpha concentration.

docs.title: Slot: total_antioxidant_capacity
docs.text: Total antioxidant capacity. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: total_cell_count
docs.text: Total cell count in BALF/sputum.

docs.title: Slot: total_egfr_protein
docs.text: Total EGFR protein level (loading control). TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: total_lung_capacity
docs.text: Total lung capacity. TIER 3 - requires more equipment.

docs.title: Slot: total_protein_concentration
docs.text: Total protein concentration.

docs.title: Slot: transport_directionality
docs.text: Directionality of mucociliary transport. TIER 1.

docs.title: Slot: transport_rate
docs.text: Mucociliary transport rate. TIER 1 - primary outcome measure for MCC assays.

docs.title: Slot: treated_output
docs.text: Reference (by id) to the AssayOutputMeasurement record for the treated group.

docs.title: Slot: unit
docs.text: The unit of measurement.

docs.title: Slot: upper_bound
docs.text: Upper bound when variability is reported as an interval (confidence interval, range, IQR).

docs.title: Slot: upstream_event
docs.text: The upstream key event in this relationship (cause).

docs.title: Slot: upstream_key_events
docs.text: Key events that lead to this key event (upstream in the pathway).

docs.title: Slot: validation_status
docs.text: Validation status of the protocol.

docs.title: Slot: value
docs.text: The numeric value of the quantity.

docs.title: Slot: variability
docs.text: The reported variability around the value (SD, SEM, confidence interval, or range), kept separate from the central value itself.

docs.title: Slot: variability_type
docs.text: The kind of variability reported (standard deviation, standard error, 95% confidence interval, range, interquartile range).
